Not all fiction is supposed to have characters that are like real people. Realism has been an increasingly popular style for the past 150 years, but lots fiction uses different paradigms. Romantic literature (not to be confused with the Romance genre of novels; think Hugo's Les Misérables) use characters to represent different ideals interacting.

Ayn Rand often gets criticized for a lack of realism in her characters, but that was due to her writing more in the Romantic tradition. I suspect there might be similar issues when people answer this question; the creators may not even be striving for realism.
